- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Epic of Gilgamesh is an ancient epic poem from Mesopotamia that tells the story of Gilgamesh, the king of Uruk.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The poem is one of the oldest surviving works of literature in the world and is considered to be a masterpiece of world literature.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The epic tells the story of Gilgamesh's journey to find the secret of immortality after the death of his friend Enkidu.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Along the way, he faces many challenges and encounters a variety of mythical creatures, including a giant snake that steals the secret of immortality from him.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite his efforts, Gilgamesh is ultimately unable to achieve immortality, but he learns about the value of friendship, the importance of living a virtuous life, and the inevitability of death.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The epic ends with Gilgamesh's acceptance of his own mortality and his return to Uruk, where he is hailed as a great king.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Epic of Gilgamesh is a powerful and enduring tale that has inspired many later works of literature and art.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Utnapishtim builds a large boat and fills it with his family, friends, and a variety of animals, and the boat rides out the storm safely.
